description: Requirement lint catalogue v1 (Keval, Sprint 0; US-51 uses it from Sprint 3). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions written in the common subset of Python `re` and JavaScript RegExp, so the composer can run them in the browser with no AI call.

entries.hint: Say how fast, e.g. "within 2 seconds for 95% of requests".

entries.message: Usability word that cannot be tested.
entries.hint: Name a measurable target, e.g. "a new user completes sign-up in under 3 minutes".
State the measure, e.g. availability, throughput, or the standard to meet.
Replace it with a number or a range.

entries.pattern: \b(if possible|as appropriate|as needed|where applicable|as far as possible|ideally|preferably|normally|usually|typically)\b
entries.message: Escape clause: when does this not apply?
entries.hint: State the condition explicitly, or remove the hedge.

entries.pattern: \b(etc\.?|and so on|and\/or|such as|including but not limited to|any other)\b
entries.hint: List every item, or point to where the full list is defined.

entries.message: Absolute word: is there really no exception?
entries.hint: Keep it only if no exception exists; otherwise name the scope.
Fill it in, or open an issue for the missing information.

entries.message: Passive voice hides who does it.
entries.hint: Name the actor: "The system shall …" or "The administrator shall …".

entries.message: No actor: who or what shall do this?
entries.hint: Start with the system, a component or a user class.
Use "shall" for mandatory behaviour; record optional behaviour with the Where… template.
